title: Two-flat gut rehab with rear porch

project.description: Interior rehabilitation of an existing two-flat and replacement of the rear porch. Zoning district RS-3. Standard Plan Review.
project.reviewer: Department of Buildings, first review cycle

comments.heading: Structural
comments.text: The rear porch framing plan does not state the design live load. Note the design loads on the plan.

comments.heading: Building
comments.text: Picket spacing at the second floor porch guard is not shown. Provide a guard detail.

comments.heading: Building
comments.text: Identify the work area and the classification of the work under the rehabilitation code in the code summary.

comments.heading: Zoning
comments.text: The new porch roof extends into the required rear yard. This needs a variation from the Zoning Board of Appeals before zoning can approve the plans.

comments.heading: Energy
comments.text: Compliance documentation for the new exterior wall insulation is not included. Provide the insulation values on the wall sections.

comments.heading: General
comments.text: Provide a current plat of survey with the application.

expected.why: Design loads are the engineer's to set. Don't propose a value.
A guard is a life-safety detail for the architect, filed under means of egress.
Classifying work under the rehabilitation code is a professional code interpretation, not paperwork.
The next step is at the Zoning Board of Appeals, not a sheet revision.
Insulation values are design data from the architect, and the Energy Transformation Code governs.
